newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary's Gardenia to seek bourse listing.
newsitem.headline: Hungary's Gardenia to seek bourse listing.

text.p: Hungarian curtain factory Gardenia Rt said on Tuesday that it planned a capital market transaction which would combine a sale of own shares and a capital increase, followed by a bourse listing.

The capital increase would raise Gardenia's issued share capital by between 600 million and one billion forints from the current one billion, Peter Zelnik, chairman of Gardenia's supervisory board, told a news conference.
The capital increase is aimed at financing the company's expansion plans, he said.
"First, we would like to build a new plant and to buy new machinery," Zelnik said. "Second, we would like to make acquisitions...in the area of home textiles."
Zelnik said the company was interested in both producing and sales companies and talks were going on in Hungary and abroad.
He also said Gardenia planned to invest a total 2.3-2.4 billion forints during 1997-99.
Company officials declined to go into details about the planned transactions but said the share issue would be public and they were seeking financial investors.

Company president and CEO Marta Polyak said Gardenia planned to generate sales revenues of four billion forints in 1997, after 3.1 billion in 1996. Gardenia's after-tax profit was between 300 million and 310 million forints in 1996, she said.
Polyak said roughly two-thirds of the company's sales stemmed from exports to over 30 countries while the remainder was generated on the domestic market.
